issues.legal_issue: A suit by a purchaser of an undivided coparcenary interest for partition and possession is not barred by limitation where the applicable limitation period has not run after an interruption of adverse possession, or where no unequivocal threat to the asserted right is shown.
material_facts: The plaintiff’s predecessor purchased the undivided shares of four coparceners at an execution sale; another coparcener had not been made a party to the sale proceedings.
A court ordered symbolic delivery of possession to the purchaser’s transferee, and that delivery was carried out.
The suit was filed within twelve years of the symbolic delivery.
There was no evidence that the defendants had unequivocally challenged the purchaser’s asserted right.
issues.conclusion: The suit was not barred by limitation, whether Article 144 or Article 120 applied.
issues.legal_principle: Article 144 of the Limitation Act concerns possession and requires the prescribed period of adverse possession; even assuming it applies to this kind of suit, symbolic delivery of possession interrupted the continuity of adverse possession, so time ran from that delivery. Article 120 applies where no other limitation period is provided and time runs when the asserted right accrues and is met by an unequivocal threat of infringement. Mst. Rukhmabai v. Lala Laxminarayan and C. Mohammad Yunus v. Syed Unnissa were relied on for the latter rule; Bai Shevantibai v. Janardan R. Warick was disapproved insofar as it treated the sale date as the accrual date. Sri Radha Krishna Chanderji v. Ram Bahadur was relied on for the interruptive effect of formal possession. Justice Ramaswami separately considered Article 144 applicable and identified the sale as the initial starting point for adverse possession, while agreeing that symbolic delivery interrupted it.

predicates.alienee_partition_possession_suit: A purchaser of an undivided coparcenary interest brought a suit seeking partition and possession of the share attributable to the seller.
predicates.symbolic_delivery_interrupted_adverse_po: A court-ordered symbolic delivery of possession was carried out in favour of the purchaser or the purchaser’s transferee, interrupting the defendants’ adverse possession.
predicates.suit_within_limitation_after_interruptio: The suit was brought before the applicable limitation period had run from the interruption of adverse possession.
predicates.no_unequivocal_threat_to_asserted_right: The defendants had not unequivocally challenged the right asserted in the suit.

issues.definition: For a purchaser’s partition-and-possession suit, the suit is not time-barred when symbolic delivery interrupts adverse possession and the suit is timely after that interruption, or when no unequivocal threat to the asserted right is shown.

issues.legal_issue: A court-ordered symbolic delivery of possession interrupts adverse possession when the court acted within its jurisdiction, even if the order was legally erroneous.
material_facts: The purchaser’s transferee obtained symbolic delivery of possession under a court order after notice to the affected defendants.
The order was carried out by publishing the delivery in the prescribed manner.
The order was not set aside, although the purchaser of an undivided coparcenary share was not legally entitled to possession at that stage.
issues.conclusion: The symbolic delivery was not a nullity and interrupted the continuity of the defendants’ adverse possession.
issues.legal_principle: An order made by a court acting within its jurisdiction has effect unless set aside, even if the court made an error of law. Whether adverse possession was interrupted turns on whether possession was in fact obtained, not on whether the delivery was legally justified. Sri Radha Krishna Chanderji v. Ram Bahadur supports the interruptive effect of formal possession. Yelumalai Chetti v. Srinivasa Chetti did not establish that the delivery order was a nullity.

predicates.alienee_partition_possession_suit: A purchaser of an undivided coparcenary interest brought a suit seeking partition and possession.
predicates.symbolic_possession_delivered_under_cour: A court ordered symbolic delivery of possession and the delivery was carried out.
predicates.order_made_within_jurisdiction: The court had jurisdiction to make the order, even though the order may have been legally erroneous.

issues.definition: In an alienee’s partition-and-possession suit, symbolic possession delivered under an order made within the court’s jurisdiction interrupts adverse possession even if the order was legally erroneous.

issues.legal_issue: An execution-sale purchaser of the shares of some coparceners is entitled only to the interests actually sold and cannot obtain the share of a coparcener whose interest was not sold.
material_facts: At the time of the execution sale, the shares of four coparceners were put up for sale.
Another son had been born before the sale but was not a party to the suit or execution proceedings, and his share was not sold.
The four sons’ shares, initially described as four-fifths, amounted to two-thirds after the additional son’s birth.
issues.conclusion: The purchaser was entitled to a two-thirds share, not a four-fifths share, and could not claim the additional son’s share.
issues.legal_principle: An execution-sale purchaser acquires the interests of the judgment-debtors that were actually put up for sale; an interest that was not sold does not pass to the purchaser. No earlier case was relied on for this determination.

predicates.partition_suit_by_execution_sale_purchas: A purchaser at an execution sale sought partition and possession of joint family property.
predicates.only_some_coparceners_interests_sold: The execution sale included the interests of only some of the coparceners.
predicates.another_coparcener_excluded_from_sale: A coparcener’s interest was not included in the sale because that coparcener was not a party to the proceedings.

issues.definition: An execution-sale purchaser seeking partition can obtain only the interests included in the sale, not the interest of a coparcener excluded from it.
